images.title: Smallest first, largest last
images.purpose: Show data arranged in ascending order with the smallest at one end, the largest at the other and equal sizes together.
images.composition: One long row of 7 equal cards centred, with a label above each end, and wide white space.
images.exact_structure: One row of exactly 7 equal square cards, evenly spaced, showing 3, 3, 4, 5, 5, 6, 6 from left to right. The first card (3) is filled teal #0072B2, the last card (6) is filled amber #E69F00, the other 5 plain. A short grey #6B7280 arrow below the row points left to right. Exactly 7 cards and 1 arrow.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
cards that are not in ascending order
images.takeaway: In ascending order the smallest comes first and the largest comes last.
images.description: A row of 7 cards 3, 3, 4, 5, 5, 6, 6 in ascending order, the first card teal as smallest and the last card amber as largest.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the smallest and largest cards and say where the equal ones sit.

image_decisions.why: Ascending order is a picture idea; one row of cards carries it.
